title: IBM’s new CEO Arvind Krishna is mastermind behind cloud strategy for growth
summary: Arvind Krishna, IBM’s new CEO, is credited with conceptualizing the company’s hybrid cloud strategy in 2017, a move that revitalized the 108-year-old tech giant. His vision led to the acquisition of Red Hat and a strategic shift towards cloud computing, similar to Satya Nadella's successful leadership at Microsoft. Analysts and former colleagues believe Krishna is well-suited to transform IBM and steer it towards future growth in the competitive tech market.

title: Goldman Sachs in talks with Amazon to offer small-business loans
summary: Goldman Sachs is reportedly close to a deal with Amazon to offer small-business loans to Amazon's U.S. customers, aiming to expand its reach onto Main Street. This move aligns with Goldman's strategy to diversify beyond trading and investment banking, while Amazon benefits by extending its lending platform without incurring significant credit risk or regulatory obligations. The partnership would leverage Goldman's financial services expertise and Amazon's vast network of small and medium-sized sellers, further solidifying both companies' ventures into new market segments.

title: IBM replaces Ginni Rometty, names Arvind Krishna as CEO
summary: IBM has named Arvind Krishna, head of the company's cloud business, as its new CEO, succeeding Ginni Rometty. The leadership change, announced on January 31, 2020, comes amidst fierce competition from Microsoft Azure and Amazon AWS, and surprised some Wall Street analysts. Krishna, credited with IBM's $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, will assume the role in April.

title: Starbucks improves customer experience with AI
summary: Starbucks is enhancing its customer experience through the deployment of AI-equipped hardware and analytics. The company plans to install 4,000 AI-enabled Mastrena II espresso makers in 2020 and is leveraging its Deep Brew AI engine to understand customer preferences better and increase efficiency. These efforts, combined with significant growth in its loyalty program and digital customer base, are contributing to improved service, brand loyalty, and new offerings.

title: Virgin Galactic Stock: A Unique High-Flying Infrastructure Stock to Watch in 2020
summary: Virgin Galactic Holdings (SPCE) is presented as a unique infrastructure stock with significant growth potential in the burgeoning space economy, estimated to reach $1.5 trillion by 2040. The company aims to be the world's first commercial spaceline, launching paying passengers into suborbital space. Despite being speculative and not yet profitable, Virgin Galactic has made progress with test flights and plans to reopen ticket sales, making it a stock worth watching for risk-tolerant investors.

title: STARZ AND LIONSGATE INK OUTPUT DEAL FOR SPLIT THEATRICAL STREAMING WINDOW IN THE UK
summary: STARZPLAY has entered a multi-year theatrical output deal with Lionsgate for split first-pay streaming rights in the UK. This agreement will bring Lionsgate's recent and upcoming feature films, including "Knives Out" and "Bombshell," to STARZPLAY subscribers just six months after their Amazon Prime Video debut in the territory. The deal aims to enhance STARZPLAY's content offering and support its international expansion.

title: Amazon Revenue vs Net Income by Quarter
summary: This article details Amazon's quarterly revenue and net income performance from Q1 1997 through Q4 2019, highlighting key financial milestones. It notes Amazon achieving a record high revenue of $87,437 million in Q4 2019 and its first profitable quarter in Q4 2001. The article also provides a brief overview of Amazon Inc., its history, and major products.

title: Are QVC and HSN Destined to Die?
summary: This article questions the future of home shopping networks QVC and HSN in an era dominated by online retail and changing consumer preferences. Despite declining stock prices and revenue, the author highlights QVC's efforts, including a merger with HSN, improved online sales, flexible payment options, and strong customer service, suggesting these strategies might help them survive. The piece ultimately expresses hope for their continued existence.

title: eBay is more like the NYSE than Amazon, says Intercontinental Exchange CEO Jeffrey Sprecher
summary: Jeffrey Sprecher, CEO of Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), argued that eBay, an e-commerce giant, more closely resembles the New York Stock Exchange than Amazon. He suggested eBay should be viewed as a 25-year-old cash market for collectible goods, emphasizing business model similarities like matching buyers and sellers, data collection, and third-party partnerships. This perspective emerged as ICE clarified its discussions with eBay, which it ultimately ceased pursuing for strategic opportunities.

title: 3 ETFs to Consider as Amazon Set to Create 15,000 Jobs
summary: Amazon plans to hire 15,000 employees in Bellevue, Washington, and build a new 43-story tower, significantly boosting the local job market. This news follows a strong private payrolls report showing 291,000 new jobs in January. The article recommends three ETFs with Amazon exposure: Fidelity MSCI Consumer Discretionary Index ETF (FDIS), Consumer Discret Sel Sect SPDR ETF (XLY), and ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN).

title: Uber is ready to join the FANG camp, analyst says after earnings
summary: Following its latest earnings report, an analyst suggested that Uber Technologies Inc. is ready to join the ranks of major internet companies like Facebook, Amazon, Netflix, and Google. RBC Capital Markets analyst Mark Mahaney proposed the acronym FANGU, adding Uber, as the company works towards profitability and leverages its scale. This optimism led to an 8% increase in Uber's stock price on Friday morning.

title: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, Named to 2020 Wash100 for Driving Revenue, Tech Advancement
summary: Matt Desch, CEO of Iridium Communications, has been inducted into the 2020 Wash100 Award for his continuous efforts in driving revenue and advancing satellite, IoT, and cloud technologies. This marks his sixth consecutive Wash100 award, highlighting his significant impact on the government contracting sector through initiatives like Iridium's L-band broadband service, partnerships with Satelles and Amazon Web Services, and authorization for GMDSS satellite services. His leadership has led to substantial growth for Iridium, including a 12 percent revenue increase in Q1 2019 and a 25 percent rise in commercial IoT data subscribers.

title: Are video games a worthwhile investment?
summary: Raj Lala, CEO of Evolve ETFs, discusses the investment potential of the video game industry, explaining why he launched the HERO ETF to provide exposure to major gaming companies. He highlights the significant evolution of the industry's revenue model beyond simple sales, citing in-app purchases, subscriptions, and esports as key drivers. Lala emphasizes that gaming fits into Evolve's strategy of investing in disruptive technologies that will shape the future and advises financial advisors to understand the full ecosystem of the market.

title: Amazon’s Total Stock-based Compensation Expense, by Quarter
summary: This article analyzes Amazon's total stock-based compensation expense by quarter from 1998, highlighting significant increases, such as $1,840 million in Q4 2019, a 29.9% year-over-year rise. It notes Amazon's substantial workforce of approximately 798,000 employees as of December 2019 and provides background on Amazon's history and key offerings.

title: Tyler Technologies Tops $1B in Annual Revenue for First Time
summary: Tyler Technologies announced its annual revenue surpassed $1 billion for the first time in 2019, reaching $1.068 billion, a 16.2 percent increase from 2018. The company, a leading provider of public sector software, expects continued double-digit growth and aims for $2 billion in annual revenue, supported by its Connected Communities vision and strategic investments in cloud technologies and acquisitions.

title: Oracle’s Larry Ellison makes friends with his enemy’s enemy, hosting a fundraiser for President Trump
summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is hosting a fundraiser for President Donald Trump, aligning with a shared adversary of Amazon and its CEO Jeff Bezos. Ellison's company has a fierce rivalry with Amazon's cloud computing wing, and Trump has openly expressed a desire to "screw Amazon." This move places Ellison among a few Silicon Valley figures who have publicly supported Trump, despite potential backlash from the tech industry.

title: How Blackstone became the world’s biggest corporate landlord
summary: Blackstone has grown to become the world's largest corporate landlord, accumulating $325 billion in real estate assets through strategic investments since going public in 2007. The firm employs both "opportunistic" (BREP) and "Core+" (BREIT) funds, focusing on distressed properties and stable rental income, respectively, while increasingly targeting warehouses in "last-mile infill" areas due to the e-commerce boom. Its ability to raise massive funds allows it to make large-scale deals with limited competition, shaping its investment strategy around fast-growing "knowledge centers."

title: This Growth ETF Continues Winning
summary: The article discusses the continued outperformance of growth stocks over value stocks in early 2020, driven by technology and consumer discretionary sectors. It highlights the SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 Growth ETF (SPYG) as a strong performer, noting its impressive year-to-date gains compared to the broader S&P 500 and S&P 500 Value Index. The piece also contrasts growth and value investing strategies and mentions significant inflows into SPYG.

title: Israeli VC Firm Grove Ventures Closes $120M Fund For Deep Tech Startups
summary: Israeli VC firm Grove Ventures announced the closure of its Grove Ventures II Fund (Grove II), raising $120 million to invest in early-stage, deep tech startups in Israel targeting European and US markets. The fund, which was oversubscribed, focuses on companies developing "hard-to-replicate solutions" across various sectors, led by serial entrepreneur Dov Moran. Grove Ventures aims to empower deep tech entrepreneurs to build international companies and address significant industry challenges with innovative technology.

title: Franklin-Legg Mason combo could produce nontransparent ETF powerhouse
summary: The pending merger of Franklin Resources and Legg Mason, while having a relatively small combined ETF asset base, could position them as a significant player in the nontransparent ETF space. This potential stems from Legg Mason's majority stake in Precidian Investments, a company licensing nontransparent ETF structures, which could give the merged entity a first-mover advantage as these new fund types are expected to launch soon. Nontransparent ETFs offer a new avenue for active mutual fund managers to enter the ETF market with potential benefits like lower costs and greater tax efficiency.

title: Piedmont Pays $396M for Dallas Galleria Office Towers
summary: Piedmont Office Realty Trust acquired the three distinctive Galleria office towers in Dallas for $396 million, marking the largest Dallas-Fort Worth office sale of the year. The transaction included over 1.4 million square feet of Class A office space, associated parking garages, and a 1.9-acre land parcel. This acquisition means Piedmont now owns the entire Galleria portfolio in Dallas, having previously acquired Galleria properties in Atlanta.

title: Beyond ESG: How Individuals Can Influence Corporations
summary: This article discusses how individuals can influence corporations beyond traditional ESG investing by leveraging their consumer choices, employment decisions, and advocacy. It highlights the rise of stakeholder capitalism and provides examples of how customers, employees, suppliers, communities, and shareholders have successfully pressured companies to adopt more responsible practices, leading to positive corporate behavior and potentially superior stock returns.

title: Expedia cuts 3,000 jobs, including 500 at new Seattle HQ — read the internal email to employees
summary: Expedia Group is laying off 3,000 employees, or 12 percent of its workforce, including 500 at its new Seattle headquarters, as part of an effort to "streamline and focus" the company under chairman Barry Diller. These cuts follow the ouster of the CEO and CFO and a commitment to address an "unhealthy and undisciplined" growth strategy, aiming for $300 to $500 million in annual cost savings. The layoffs are not linked to the coronavirus outbreak, though the company expects related profit reductions and will incur $135 million to $185 million in pre-tax charges this year.

title: Checkup for $30, Teeth Cleaning $25: Walmart Gets Into Health Care
summary: Walmart is entering the healthcare market by offering low-cost medical services such as $30 checkups and $25 teeth cleanings in its new Walmart Health centers. This initiative aims to capture a share of the $3.6 trillion health spending by leveraging its large customer base and providing accessible care, even for those without insurance. The retail giant's move positions it as a competitor to existing healthcare providers like CVS and Amazon in communities nationwide.

title: Comcast acquires free video streaming service Xumo
summary: Comcast announced its acquisition of Xumo, a free, ad-supported streaming service, positioning itself to compete in the growing ad-supported streaming market. This strategic move comes ahead of NBCUniversal's launch of its own streaming service, Peacock, which will also offer free, ad-supported content. The acquisition highlights the increasing trend of media companies investing in streaming services as consumers shift away from traditional pay TV.

title: Kraft Heinz invests in $110m Series B for cloud retail robotics startup Fabric
summary: Kraft Heinz, through its venture arm Evolv Ventures, invested in a $110 million Series B round for the cloud retail robotics startup Fabric. Fabric's technology provides automated fulfillment solutions for retailers facing increasing demand for fast e-commerce delivery. The funding will support Fabric's US expansion, aiming to address the challenges retailers face in efficient order fulfillment.

title: Prudential buys local Amazon distribution hub
summary: PGIM Real Estate, a branch of Prudential, has acquired a new Amazon distribution hub located in Antioch, Nashville. This 517,500-square-foot industrial building was developed speculatively, indicating strong confidence in the demand for industrial space in the Nashville market. Amazon is the current tenant, leasing the facility.

title: Walmart is developing a membership program to rival Amazon Prime
summary: Walmart Inc. is developing a new paid membership program called Walmart+ to compete directly with Amazon Prime. This service will expand on Walmart's existing grocery-delivery subscription and aims to attract and retain shoppers who might otherwise turn to Amazon. The initiative highlights Walmart's efforts to counter Amazon's dominance in online retail and customer loyalty.
